planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Ruby Wine is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series, with deep wine-red double flowers blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Ruby Wine is part of the acclaimed Winter Jewels hellebore breeding series, producing full, rounded double flowers in a deep, glossy wine-red that darkens further with age, held above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often through late-season snow or hard frost, giving reliable color in the shade garden when little else is flowering. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to best showcase the nodding flowers, which are often tilted upright by gardeners or planted on a slope so their beauty can be appreciated without bending down. Site it away from areas where pets or children graze, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
sources: Northwest Garden Nursery — Winter Jewels hellebore breeding

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Sparkling Diamond is part of the acclaimed Winter Jewels hellebore breeding series, producing crisp, pure white, fully double flowers that catch light beautifully in a shaded border, held above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often through late-season snow or hard frost, providing bright color in the shade garden at a time when little else is flowering. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to best showcase the flowers, and consider planting on a slight slope or raised bed so the nodding blooms are easier to view and appreciate from above. Site it away from areas where pets or children graze, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.

common_name: Blue Lady Hellebore (Classic Slate-Blue Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Blue Lady is an older, well-established hellebore selection with slate-blue to purple-gray single flowers blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Blue Lady is a long-cultivated hellebore selection valued for its unusual slate-blue to smoky purple-gray single flowers, a cooler and more muted tone than the pinks, reds, and whites more commonly seen in Lenten rose selections, held above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often through late-season snow or hard frost, providing reliable color in the shade garden when little else is flowering. Its subdued, smoky coloring pairs especially well with silver-leaved companions like brunnera or lamium in a woodland border. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to showcase the flowers, and site it away from areas where pets or children graze, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
